Related: #2208

I wrote a manpages picker for mini.pick. Here it is in action:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32866873-d91e-43a7-9aea-8ab6e42721e7

Code:

```lua
--- Man pages picker
---
--- Pick from system manpages.
---
---@param local_opts __extra_pickers_local_opts
---   Possible fields:
---   - <scope> `(string)` - one of "all" (all man sections) or section string.
---     Default: "all".
---@param opts __extra_pickers_opts
MiniExtra.pickers.man = function(local_opts, opts)
  local pick = H.validate_pick("man")
  local_opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", { scope = "all" }, local_opts or {})

  local load_man = function(item)
    local keyword, cmd, section, desc = item:match("^((.-)%s*%(([^)]+)%).-)%s+%-%s+(.*)$")
    local width = vim.api.nvim_win_get_width(0)
    cmd = vim.split(cmd, ",")[1]
    vim.cmd(string.format("silent re! 2>&- MANWIDTH=%s man %s %s", width, section, cmd))
    vim.cmd("Man!")
    vim.cmd("norm gg0")
  end

  local choose = function(item, splitmode)
    vim.cmd(splitmode or "new")
    load_man(item)
    local win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
    vim.schedule(function() vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(win) end)
  end

  local preview = function(buf_id, item)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_call(buf_id, function() load_man(item) end)
  end

  local map_custom = function(char, splitmode)
    local f = function()
      choose(pick.get_picker_matches().current, splitmode)
      return true
    end
    return { char = char, func = f }
  end

  local conf_maps = pick.config.mappings
  local mappings = {
    choose_in_split   = "", show_man_in_split   = map_custom(conf_maps.choose_in_split, "new"),
    choose_in_vsplit  = "", show_man_in_vsplit  = map_custom(conf_maps.choose_in_vsplit, "vnew"),
    choose_in_tabpage = "", show_man_in_tabpage = map_custom(conf_maps.choose_in_tabpage, "tabnew"),
  }

  local cmd = { "man", "-kls", local_opts.scope == "all" and "" or local_opts.scope, "" }
  local source = { name = "Manpages", choose = choose, preview = preview }
  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", { source = source, mappings = mappings }, opts or {})
  return pick.builtin.cli({ command = cmd }, opts)
end
```

~~It is currently written as a `builtin` picker, which was made clear in #2208 that it won't be. If it is decided, that it would be accepted into mini.extra, I would rewrite it for that purpouse.~~ Rewritten as mini.extra picker. That wasn't hard at all lol.

comment_data.body: I ran into so many problems with man pages while trying to rewrite your code using the `:Man` command directly: 1. ~~Man pages are not restored between sessions, even though the window keeps its name.~~ Does work as expected from time to time. 2. Opening a man page in a small window prints escape sequences and occasionally produces errors. 3. Using `:hide Man {page} {name}` reuses an existing buffer with all the artifacts and the same wrapping (`vim.g.man_hardwrap = 1` by default), even if the buffer is empty (see p.1). Soft wrapping doesn’t really help because of p.2, and some pages look bad anyway (for example, `Tcl`). So, running `man` as an external command makes sense to me. Other: - Man pages are very slow to open, especially large ones like `tmux` (which is relevant for the preview). - Personally, I would use `man -k`, since it is easier for me to understand.
comment_data.bodyHTML:
I ran into so many problems with man pages while trying to rewrite your code using the :Man command directly:

  1. Man pages are not restored between sessions, even though the window keeps its name. Does work as expected from time to time.
  2. Opening a man page in a small window prints escape sequences and occasionally produces errors.
  3. Using :hide Man {page} {name} reuses an existing buffer with all the artifacts and the same wrapping (vim.g.man_hardwrap = 1 by default), even if the buffer is empty (see p.1). Soft wrapping doesn’t really help because of p.2, and some pages look bad anyway (for example, Tcl).

So, running man as an external command makes sense to me.

Other:

  • Man pages are very slow to open, especially large ones like tmux (which is relevant for the preview).
  • Personally, I would use man -k, since it is easier for me to understand.

I ran into so many problems with man pages while trying to rewrite your code using the :Man command directly:

Man pages are not restored between sessions, even though the window keeps its name. Does work as expected from time to time.
Opening a man page in a small window prints escape sequences and occasionally produces errors.
Using :hide Man {page} {name} reuses an existing buffer with all the artifacts and the same wrapping (vim.g.man_hardwrap = 1 by default), even if the buffer is empty (see p.1). Soft wrapping doesn’t really help because of p.2, and some pages look bad anyway (for example, Tcl).

So, running man as an external command makes sense to me.

Other:

Man pages are very slow to open, especially large ones like tmux (which is relevant for the preview).
Personally, I would use man -k, since it is easier for me to understand.

Even extremely large manpages like gcc's open in less than half a second for me. I don't know what's causing the issue for you. Have you tried comparing just regular `man tmux` and the picker preview?

> session

Yes, you're right that does appear to be broken. I'll try fiddling with `sessionopts`, see if that fixes it.

I edited the function to use `man -k` and the `-l` option. Thanks for spotting that.
